newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says 1996 loss will be significant.
newsitem.headline: Renault says 1996 loss will be significant.

text.p: Renault said on Thursday that its 1996 results would be "significantly" negative in a statement announcing a plant closure in Belgium to streamline its industrial facilities.

"In 1996, for the first time in 10 years, Renault's consolidated results will be negative and quite significantly so," the company said. "This situation cannot be allowed to continue without it constituting a major danger for the company."

After Renault's most recent profit warning earlier this month, analysts cut their estimates for a full-year loss of around two billion francs ($351.3 million) for 1996. The newspaper Les Echos said the loss may be twice that amount after restructuring charges.
Renault said in its statement that it was essential to take "rapid corrective action".

"One of the key measures Renault is taking to improve the company's competitiveness is to implement an industrial strategy based on dedicated production units and plant rationalisation, in a move to make optimum use of its production capacity," it said.
Renault said it was looking for a buyer for its Renault Industrie Belgique (RIB) plant and planned to halt production there in July.
It said 3,100 people were employed at RIB and their output could be matched by the equivalent of 1,900 jobs at other plants because the Renault group is not producing at full capacity.

"RIB currently assembles the Renault Megane and Renault Clio models (output of 143,342 vehicles in 1996). It is possible to concentrate production of the Megane at the Douai plant in northern France and the Palencia plant in Spain," it said.

"The Laguna can be produced in a single location at the Sandouville site in France. In addition, by increasing the workload at Palencia and transferring production work on the Clio which is currently carried out at the RIB plant, it is possible to focus Twingo production in a single site at Flins in France," it said.

Renault said its industrial base in Europe was too diffuse and inefficient. "This situation has generated a high degree of complexity, notably for equipment, manufacturing processes and logistics and has resulted in higher capital spending and greater production costs," it said.

"Circumstances require an acceleration of the rate of progress being made in our cost reduction programme, in order to put the company in a strong position to confront more aggressive competition in a more open market," it said.
It said it was committed to taking measures to give each worker at RIB "the best possible chance of finding a new job".

The Socialist-led CFDT union issued a statement calling the Belgian plant closure "an incredible brutality". The union said it would work with its Belgian counterparts to force the company to abandon the plan.
